messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up, launching a config-only push for routing weights + tinybatch and idle-timeout during the 2200-2300 UTC change window. No code changes.
deploy-bot: @Maya Chen: Change request queued: cfg-2026-03-routing-slim. ETA start 2026-03-21 22:00 UTC. Approvals: auto (eng-releases).
Samir Patel: ACK. I’ll be on watch. Tracking checklist: monitoring, canary 5%, pin fallback, rollback steps.
Rajesh Kumar: Pin request: leave model v1.9.3 pinned for 15m after rollout. If latency > 99th baseline + 60ms, rollback immediately.
Elaine Yu: I pushed a short dashboard: /dashboards/latency/cfg-2026-03-routing-slim — will alert on p95 and error spike.
Maya Chen: Config yaml I’m applying (snippet):
```yaml
routing:
  default_weight: 0.85
  fallback_weight: 0.15
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  tiny_batch_threshold: 8
timeouts:
  idle_ms: 45
  req_timeout_ms: 22000
```
Samir Patel: Quick q: tiny_batch_threshold 8 okay for async tenants? Might spike cold-starts. Suggest keeping a soft ramp.
Maya Chen: Good call — adding ramp: soft_ramp: { "step_secs": 300, "delta": 2 } in the full config.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: cfg-2026-03-routing-slim -> canary group A (5%). Logs: https://ci.redwood/changes/cfg-2026-03-routing-slim
Samir Patel: Canary live. Watching token cost, tail latency. @Elaine please confirm traces are flowing.
Elaine Yu: Traces OK. p95 looks stable so far. p99 small bump +12ms (expected). No errors.
Rajesh Kumar: Reminder: pin fallback should be model v1.9.3 -> v1.9.1 in the rollback script. Script: `scripts/rollback_pin.sh cfg-2026-03-routing-slim v1.9.1`
Maya Chen: Increasing to 25% after 10 minutes if stable. If p95 <= baseline + 10ms and error rate stable.
deploy-bot: Canary scaled to 25%.
Samir Patel: Noticing slight KV-cache pressure on host pool r4. Plan: reduce max_batch_tokens to 1536 for the next cohort.
Maya Chen: Applying cohort tweak now — small config patch pushed to cohort B.
Elaine Yu: Metrics: CPU on r4 trending up 6%, mem steady. No OOM. Logs show a few `kvcache-miss` warnings but within threshold.
Rajesh Kumar: If kvcache misses > 0.4% over 5m, we rollback batch change. Set alarm.
Maya Chen: Alarm set. Also updated release notes summary: "Config-only: route weight shift to prioritize low-latency path, tiny-batching enabled, idle timeout reduced to 45ms, small batch cap lowered for PK-sensitive tenants."
Samir Patel: Adding ops note: tenants with async-heavy traffic should be excluded from tiny-batching — I’ll create tenant-exclude tag: `tinybatch: exclude` for the known ones.
deploy-bot: Rollout at 90% scheduled in 20 minutes if no alerts.
Elaine Yu: Adding canary traces to the perf-regression suite for automated replay.
Maya Chen: 10m to 90% check. Anyone see anything blocking?
Samir Patel: All good here.
Rajesh Kumar: Watch the fallback path latency if traffic gets routed there — it can be 30-40ms higher.
Maya Chen: Understood. If p99 > baseline + 80ms we trigger immediate rollback.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused: automated alert — p99 exceeded threshold on routing-fallback cluster at 1733340155.
Maya Chen: Rolling back batch cap change only to previous value (2048) for affected clusters. Running: `kubectl apply -f rollback-batchcap-cohortB.yaml`
Samir Patel: Patch applied, confirming config propagation.
Elaine Yu: Post-fix metrics: p99 dropping back toward baseline. kvcache misses decreasing. No new errors.
deploy-bot: Deploy update: cohort B batchcap reverted; rollout resumed to 90%.
Maya Chen: We’ll keep the route weight and idle timeout but revert the lower batch cap for now. Note: need a follow-up RFC to test tiny-batching with async tenants.
Rajesh Kumar: Logged the postmortem item and pinned fallback version to v1.9.3 for the next 30m.
Samir Patel: Thx all. I’ll update the release notes and tag the rollback entry. :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: Closing window — rollout completed to 100% at 2026-03-21 23:00 UTC. Marking as stable.
deploy-bot: Change cfg-2026-03-routing-slim completed. Summary: partial revert (batch cap), route weight + idle timeout applied, tiny-batching schedule deferred for async tenants.
Elaine Yu: Final check: histograms stable, cost delta +1.2% (expected).
Maya Chen: Great. Follow-ups: RFC for tiny-batching async plan, tenant-exclude tags, monitor retention policy. Thanks everyone.
